title: PCSX2 gives Big Picture Mode stick navigation without diagonal focus jumps
summary: Analog axes now feed cardinal ImGui navigation events, deliberately rejecting diagonal movement that could produce accidental sidebar or grid transitions.
heroAlt: Source evidence from PCSX2 pull request #14228: FullscreenUI: Add analog control to big picture mode

sourceLabels.pcsx2-pr-14228: FullscreenUI: Add analog control to big picture mode

blocks.text: D-pad-only navigation is reliable but not every user's preference

Big Picture Mode is designed for controller use, yet its menu navigation originally depended on D-pad inputs. Users accustomed to modern console interfaces often expect a left or right stick to move through game tiles and settings. Simply enabling ImGui's built-in analog navigation was not sufficient because analog values also influenced sidebar behavior and could move focus in ways that did not match PCSX2's layout.
Stick axes are translated into the established D-pad event path

Pull request #14228 listens to left- and right-stick axes through InputManager and the SDL and XInput sources, then emits ImGui cardinal navigation inputs. The menu therefore reuses the same focus rules already exercised by D-pad users instead of introducing a second analog cursor model. Supporting both sticks also avoids assuming one universal accessibility or controller preference.
Diagonal input is deliberately treated as no movement

When both axes cross their direction thresholds, PCSX2 suppresses the navigation event. That may seem stricter than choosing the dominant axis, but it prevents a diagonal hold from alternating between rows, columns, or sidebars as values fluctuate. The same rule applies to a D-pad capable of reporting diagonal combinations, keeping menu focus deterministic across input devices.
Held axes and threshold crossings need longer tests than single taps

Navigate every Big Picture grid, list, sidebar, and settings panel with each stick, verifying repeat timing and direction. Hold a diagonal and confirm no focus movement, then roll smoothly into one cardinal direction and confirm navigation begins once only that axis remains active. Repeat with SDL, XInput, dead-zone drift, and a diagonal-capable D-pad. Existing D-pad navigation, text entry, and in-game controller input must remain unchanged.
PCSX2 adds stick convenience by translating into known D-pad semantics; refusing diagonals is the mechanism that keeps focus predictable.
